sentences.text: Saltopus is a genus of very small bipedal dinosauriforms.
This animal possessed hollow bones similar to those found in birds and other dinosaurs.
It may have weighed around 1 kg.
In 2011, researchers established that the sacrum consists of only two vertebrae, representing the primitive ancestral condition rather than four.
Friedrich von Huene named and described the species as Saltopus elginensis in 1910.
The holotype was excavated from the Lossiemouth Sandstone Formation.
Saltopus has been variously classified as a saurischian dinosaur, an advanced theropod, or a relative of herrerasaurs, though its taxonomy remains disputed due to fragmentary remains.
Saltopus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
Rauhut and Hungerbühler concluded in 2000 that Saltopus is a primitive dinosauriform closely related to Lagosuchus, not a true dinosaur.
Michael Benton concluded in 2011 that Saltopus is a dinosauriform more derived than Pseudolagosuchus but outside the clade containing Silesauridae and Dinosauria.
